/-!
# Conjecture 7.19

by F. B. Cannonito

Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

By Kuznetsov's theorem the word problem of a finitely presented simple group is
always decidable, so the content of the problem is the failure of primitive
recursiveness. The requirement that the example be explicit cannot be expressed
in Lean, so we state the existence of such a group.

A finitely presented group is given as `PresentedGroup rels` with generators
indexed by `Fin n` and a finite set `rels` of relators in `FreeGroup (Fin n)`.
A word is a list `w : List (Fin n × Bool)`, where `(i, true)` denotes $x_i$ and
`(i, false)` denotes $x_i^{-1}$; `FreeGroup.mk w` is its value in the free group.
The word problem is the predicate asking whether `w` represents the identity.
It is solvable by a primitive recursive function when it is a `PrimrecPred`
with respect to Mathlib's standard coding of `List (Fin n × Bool)` by natural
numbers. This does not depend on the chosen finite presentation, since a change
of finite presentation is a primitive recursive reduction.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.19» :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
      IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup rels) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

Stated as an existence statement: there are $n$ and a finite set of relators
$R \subseteq F(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ such that the group
$G = \langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ is simple and the word problem of
$G$, i.e. the predicate on words $w$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ asking whether
$w = 1$ in $G$, is not primitive recursive.

claims.decomposer_note: Formalize as the existence Prop: there is a finitely presented (finitely many generators and relators, e.g. `PresentedGroup rels` with finite index type and finite `rels`) simple group `G` (`IsSimpleGroup`, so in particular nontrivial) such that the characteristic function of its word problem, i.e. w ↦ decide (⟦w⟧ = 1) on `FreeGroup (Fin n)` under a primitive-recursive coding of words, is not `Primrec`; the word 'explicit' cannot be captured in Lean, and by Kuznetsov's theorem the word problem is always decidable, so the content is solely the failure of primitive recursiveness (independent of the finite presentation chosen, since changing presentation is a primitive recursive reduction).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical proposition (∃ n, finite relators, IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup rels), ¬ PrimrecPred of the word problem on List (Fin n × Bool) under Mathlib's standard Primcodable coding). Verified: PrimrecPred is existential over the DecidablePred instance in this Mathlib, so ¬ PrimrecPred means exactly 'no primitive recursive characteristic function'; IsSimpleGroup extends Nontrivial, so n = 0 (trivial group) is not a degenerate witness; Primcodable instances for List/Prod/Fin/Bool exist; PresentedGroup.mk : FreeGroup α →* PresentedGroup rels. Chose c05's Set + rels.Finite form (shared with c01, c07) over the Finset form (c02, c03, c04, c06, c08) to avoid three repeated coercions; docstrings tightened. c08's extra `research solved` Kuznetsov declaration was dropped because it is not a slot.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.19

by F. B. Cannonito

Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

By Kuznetsov's theorem the word problem of a finitely presented simple group is
always decidable, so the content of the problem is the failure of primitive
recursiveness. The requirement that the example be explicit cannot be expressed

indexed by `Fin n` and a finite set `rels` of relators in `FreeGroup (Fin n)`.
A word is a list `w : List (Fin n × Bool)`, where `(i, true)` denotes $x_i$ and
`(i, false)` denotes $x_i^{-1}$; `FreeGroup.mk w` is its value in the free group.
The word problem is the predicate asking whether `w` represents the identity.
It is solvable by a primitive recursive function when it is a `PrimrecPred`
with respect to Mathlib's standard coding of `List (Fin n × Bool)` by natural

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.19»

/--
Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

Stated as an existence statement: there are $n$ and a finite set of relators
$R \subseteq F(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ such that the group
$G = \langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid R \rangle$ is simple and the word problem of
$G$, i.e. the predicate on words $w$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ asking whether
$w = 1$ in $G$, is not primitive recursive.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.19» :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
      IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup rels) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.19»

items: The problem is a construction request ('Construct an explicit example ...'), not a yes/no question, so it is stated as a plain existence theorem `∃ ...` rather than with `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`, following the decomposition table and CONTRIBUTING's guidance for non-question statements. 'Explicit' is not captured.

Finitely presented group is modelled as `PresentedGroup rels` with generators `Fin n` and `rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))` with `rels.Finite` (rather than a `Finset`, since `PresentedGroup` takes a `Set`).

The word problem is taken as a predicate on words `w : List (Fin n × Bool)` (letters x_i^{±1}), mapped to the group by `PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w)`, coded by the standard `Primcodable (List (Fin n × Bool))` instance. This is the classical input format of the word problem; the decomposition note speaks of `FreeGroup (Fin n)` under a primitive-recursive coding, and the two are equivalent since free reduction is primitive recursive. Using raw words avoids having to pick an ad hoc `Primcodable` instance on `FreeGroup (Fin n)`.

'Not solvable by a primitive recursive function' is rendered as `¬ PrimrecPred p`, where Mathlib's `PrimrecPred p := ∃ (_ : DecidablePred p), Primrec fun a => decide (p a)`; since `decide` is independent of the decidability instance up to propositional equality, this is exactly 'the characteristic function is not primitive recursive'.
Only the failure of primitive recursiveness is asserted; decidability (Kuznetsov's theorem) is not restated since it holds automatically for f.p. simple groups.
AMS tags `3 20` (mathematical logic/computability and group theory).

reviewer_notes: The source is an imperative construction request ('Construct an explicit example ...'), not a yes/no question, so per CONTRIBUTING the statement is a plain existence theorem `∃ ...` rather than `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`; the notion of 'explicit' has no Lean counterpart and is documented as dropped. Kuznetsov's theorem (decidability of the word problem of f.p. simple groups) is mentioned in the docstring as context only, not encoded. Word problem is taken on unreduced signed words List (Fin n × Bool) via FreeGroup.mk rather than on FreeGroup (Fin n) (no Primcodable instance for FreeGroup in Mathlib); free reduction is primitive recursive so this is equivalent, as is independence from the chosen finite presentation. AMS tags 3 (logic/computability) and 20 (group theory). No candidate omitted the slot and no objections to the decomposition were raised.
